story: S001: Core Hook Data Types and Matching
story_description: Implement foundational data structures for hook configuration including pattern matchers that determine when hooks fire based on tool names, event types, or custom patterns. These matchers form the core decision logic enabling hooks to target specific tools or events.
task_description: Create HookMatcher struct and MatcherType enum providing exact, multiple, wildcard, and regex pattern matching capabilities for tool names and events. Include specialized matchers for SessionStart and PreCompact events, plus intelligent pattern suggestions.
atom_description: Implement complete pattern matching infrastructure in HookMatchers.swift including HookMatcher struct with automatic type detection, MatcherType enum with four matching strategies (exact, multiple, wildcard, regex), SessionStartMatcher enum for session lifecycle events, PreCompactMatcher enum for compaction triggers, and MatcherSuggestions helper providing context-aware pattern recommendations.
problem_statement: Hooks need a flexible pattern matching system to determine when they should fire. A hook targeting Write operations should not fire for Read operations. A hook for session startup should not fire on resume. Currently there is no pattern matching infrastructure. We need a comprehensive matcher system that supports exact tool name matching, pipe-delimited multiple tool matching, wildcard matching for all tools, and regex matching for complex patterns like MCP tool namespaces. Additionally, event-specific matchers for SessionStart and PreCompact events require dedicated enum types with semantic meaning.

assumptions: Pipe character (|) is never used in actual tool names, making it safe as a delimiter
Tool names from Claude Code are stable strings matching documented names
Regex patterns use NSRegularExpression syntax (ICU regular expressions)
All matchers operate synchronously without async requirements
SessionStart event types from CLI match the four defined cases exactly
PreCompact trigger types are limited to manual user action or automatic threshold
constraints: Must use Foundation NSRegularExpression for regex matching, no third-party regex libraries
All types must be Sendable for actor isolation in HookRunner
Regex compilation errors must not crash; invalid patterns should return false for matches
Pattern detection must be deterministic and not depend on external state
All enums must be String-backed for clean JSON serialization
Must support macOS 13.0+ minimum deployment target
No heap allocation in hot path for matches() method where possible
functional_requirements: FR1: HookMatcher shall store pattern as String property accessible for UI display
FR2: HookMatcher shall store type as MatcherType property computed on initialization
FR3: HookMatcher.init(pattern:) shall call MatcherType.detect(from:) to set type automatically
FR4: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true for exact match when type is .exact and pattern equals input
FR5: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true for multiple match when type is .multiple and any pipe-delimited option equals input
FR6: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true unconditionally when type is .wildcard
FR7: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return true when type is .regex and pattern matches input via NSRegularExpression
FR8: HookMatcher.matches(_:) shall return false for .regex when pattern is invalid rather than throwing
FR9: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .wildcard for pattern exactly equal to asterisk
FR10: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .multiple for pattern containing pipe character
FR11: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .regex for pattern containing .*, [, or backslash characters
FR12: MatcherType.detect(from:) shall return .exact for all other patterns
FR13: MatcherType.displayName shall return human-readable string: Exact, Multiple, All, or Regex
FR14: MatcherType.icon shall return SF Symbol name for UI: equal, list.bullet, asterisk, or chevron.left.forwardslash.chevron.right
FR15: SessionStartMatcher shall have cases: startup, resume, clear, compact with String rawValue
FR16: SessionStartMatcher.description shall return human-readable explanation of when each fires
FR17: PreCompactMatcher shall have cases: manual, auto with String rawValue
FR18: PreCompactMatcher.description shall return human-readable explanation of trigger type
FR19: MatcherSuggestions.toolPatterns shall provide at least 10 common tool patterns with descriptions
FR20: MatcherSuggestions.suggestions(for:) shall return toolPatterns for PreToolUse and PostToolUse events
FR21: MatcherSuggestions.suggestions(for:) shall return SessionStartMatcher.allCases for SessionStart event
FR22: MatcherSuggestions.suggestions(for:) shall return PreCompactMatcher.allCases for PreCompact event
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: HookMatcher.matches() shall complete in under 1ms for exact and multiple types
NFR2: HookMatcher.matches() shall complete in under 10ms for regex patterns of reasonable length
NFR3: MatcherType.detect() shall complete in under 100 microseconds
NFR4: Memory overhead per HookMatcher instance shall not exceed 256 bytes
NFR5: All types shall be thread-safe via Sendable conformance with no mutable shared state

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty pattern string passed to HookMatcher.init - detected as exact, matches only empty string (unusual but valid)
Edge case 2: Pattern with only pipe character | - detected as multiple, splits to empty strings, matches empty tool name
Edge case 3: Pattern asterisk in middle like Read*Write - detected as regex due to *, not wildcard
Edge case 4: Invalid regex pattern like [unclosed - matches() returns false, does not throw
Edge case 5: Pattern with escaped pipe like Read\|Write - detected as regex due to backslash, matches literal Read|Write
Edge case 6: Tool name with special regex characters like mcp__fs__read - matched correctly by exact pattern
Edge case 7: Extremely long pattern (1000+ characters) - may cause regex compilation slowdown, but functions correctly
Edge case 8: Unicode characters in pattern or tool name - handled by NSRegularExpression, matches correctly
Edge case 9: Case sensitivity - matching is case-sensitive, Write does not match write
Edge case 10: Pattern with newlines or whitespace - preserved in pattern, matched literally
failure_modes: FM1: Regex pattern causes catastrophic backtracking - mitigated by NSRegularExpression timeout; matches() may return false after timeout
FM2: Pattern contains characters invalid for JSON encoding - Codable encoding fails; caller must validate input
FM3: MatcherType.detect misclassifies pattern with accidental regex chars - user gets unexpected matches; document detection rules
FM4: SessionStartMatcher raw value changes between versions - JSON deserialization fails for saved configs; maintain backward compatibility
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookMatchers.swift. Remove any imports of HookMatchers types from other files. Types are foundational but have no persistent state. Rollback requires updating any code that depends on these types to use alternative matching logic.

notes: Pattern matching is fundamental to hook targeting. The four matcher types cover common use cases: exact for single tool, multiple for tool groups, wildcard for global hooks, regex for namespaced tools like MCP. The detection heuristic prioritizes user convenience - users write Read|Write and it just works without explicit type selection.

risks: Risk 1: Regex pattern with catastrophic backtracking causes UI freeze during hook evaluation
Risk 2: Detection heuristic misclassifies intentional exact pattern containing special characters
Risk 3: SessionStartMatcher cases do not match actual CLI event strings, causing hooks to never fire
Risk 4: Future CLI versions add new event types not covered by current enums
mitigations: Mitigation 1: NSRegularExpression has built-in timeout; add explicit check and log warning for slow patterns
Mitigation 2: Document detection rules clearly; consider optional explicit type parameter in future
Mitigation 3: Verify SessionStartMatcher rawValues against actual Claude Code event strings before release
Mitigation 4: Use String-based matching with enum for known types, fallback for unknown
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to hook matching logic. Incorrect matching means hooks fire or do not fire unexpectedly. No data loss or security implications. User can adjust patterns to fix.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If pattern matching proves problematic, simplify to exact-only matching initially. Users can list multiple hooks instead of using multiple or regex patterns. Document limitations clearly.
